claims.claim_vi: Traditionally only JavaScript could be used in the browser, and its performance cannot compare with native code such as C/C++ because it is interpreted (the source wording).

claims.claim_vi: With WASM, existing native libraries written in C/C++/Rust can run in the browser with near-native performance; for example a C++ video encoding/decoding library.

claims.claim_vi: This opens possibilities for cloud computing and edge computing: serverless applications with fewer resources and instant startup time (the source claim).

claims.claim_vi: WebAssembly is a compilation target for languages like C/C++ and Rust, brings near-native performance and is designed to complement and run alongside JavaScript.

design_notes_vi: Hình gồm đường đi của mã bốn bước, thẻ trước và sau, và ba giới hạn. Ý về serverless và khởi động tức thì chỉ nêu như nhận định của nguồn. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source explains the JavaScript performance gap by saying it is interpreted; the lesson keeps this as the source wording and uses MDN wording (intensive use cases) in its own text.
Source does not mention the compile step, JavaScript loading the module, or that Wasm cannot access the DOM directly; the lesson adds them from MDN.
The serverless and edge computing claims are the source's and were not checked.
Source says the code is compiled to WASM; the lesson says it is usually compiled and may in principle be written in the text format, following MDN.
